Antigravity spans three real, distinct local products sharing the parent `~/.gemini` namespace, all confirmed present on this machine: `~/.gemini/antigravity/` (the IDE), `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` (the CLI, aka `agy`), `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/`. This explains exactly why four independent sources (CodeBurn's two providers, `agent-session-parser`, `ccusage`'s Gemini adapter reading `~/.gemini/tmp/`) all disagreed -- each was written against a different product/era in a fast-moving transition, not this current shape. This machine's session data (dated late July/August 2026) is post-transition, current ground truth.

**The `~/.gemini/logs/*.jsonl` files earlier flagged as "provenance unconfirmed" are literally symlinks**, confirmed via `ls -la`: `~/.gemini/logs/<conversation-id>.jsonl -> ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`. `logs/` is a convenience flattening layer, not a source of truth in its own right -- adapters should target the `brain/` path.

**Real transcript.jsonl schema, read directly (not inferred)**: one JSON object per line, fields `step_index` (int), `source` (`USER_EXPLICIT` | `MODEL`), `type` (a rich per-action enum: `USER_INPUT`, `LIST_DIRECTORY`, `VIEW_FILE`, `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, others uncatalogued), `status` (`DONE`, others uncatalogued), `created_at` (ISO 8601), `content` (text; for tool-action entries, this is the serialized tool result, not a separate structured result field). `PLANNER_RESPONSE` entries additionally carry `thinking` (reasoning text) and `tool_calls[]` (`name` + `args`, with `args` values themselves JSON-encoded as strings, e.g. `"args":{"DirectoryPath":"\"/Users/gabe/...\""}` -- double-encoded, a real parsing gotcha). This is structurally an Action/Observation-per-type-class model (closer to OpenHands' native model, `type` names the operation, not the message role) -- NOT the `step_index`/`source`/`type` triple in the shape Lumen's existing `AgyAdapter`/`detect_orchestrator` code was built against; the field *names* happen to overlap but the *value vocabulary* was never actually enumerated before now and needs to be checked against the adapter's current match arms.

**Two more real, distinct file shapes for the same conversation, previously unknown:** (1) a sibling `<id>.json` (no `l`) file -- a single JSON object with `sessionId`/`title`/`prompt`/`summary`/`turns[]`, where each turn is `{role, parts: [{text}]}` -- this is the standard Gemini API `Content`/`Part` shape, a precomputed summary/index view, structurally different from the raw `transcript.jsonl` and likely easier to parse if only turn-level (not full tool-call) fidelity is needed. (2) `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/history.jsonl` -- a flat *command-input* history log (`display`, `timestamp` as epoch-millis, `workspace`, `conversationId`, optional `type:"slash_command"`), NOT a conversation transcript -- a third, unrelated artifact type in the same product, useful only for correlating raw user keystrokes/slash-commands to a `conversationId`, not for turn/token reconstruction.

## Pricing architecture decision, 2026-08-20 -- the "exchange rate" model

User proposed, and this is now the settled design direction: **accumulators/adapters should only ever store raw usage data (token counts per category, model name as reported, timestamp) -- never a computed cost.** Cost is derived downstream via a lookup against a **versioned rate table**: rows of `(model, token_type, provider?, rate_per_unit, effective_from, effective_until_nullable)`, looked up by **the turn's own timestamp, not "now"** -- exactly like looking up a historical FX rate for a past transaction, not today's rate. This directly resolves two things found in this research wave, not a novel idea invented in isolation: Langfuse's real schema already separates raw `usage_details`/`cost_details` (open maps) from a separate queryable `Model`/`Price`/`PricingTier` table; `ccusage`'s Kimi adapter already has to do a timestamp-gated cutoff for one specific case (`KIMI_FOR_CODING_K2_6_CUTOFF_MS`) precisely because it lacks a general versioned-rate mechanism and has to hand-code the cutoff instead. This is the general form of that same problem. Practical implications for the redesign: (1) keep any provider-reported cost field (e.g. Claude Code's real `costUSD`) alongside the independently-computed one, not instead of it, mirroring Langfuse's `provided_*`-raw-vs-canonicalized twin-field pattern, so the two can be cross-checked for drift; (2) `pricing.rs`'s fix is this architectural separation, not just refreshed numbers -- the current hardcoded match-statement can't represent a rate change over time at all, which is a real, now-confirmed-necessary case, not a hypothetical one; (3) OpenRouter/LiteLLM's live feeds (already researched) become periodic snapshot sources that insert new `effective_from`-stamped rows, never overwrite old ones -- this is what makes historical cost analysis correct even after a provider changes prices.

- Real OpenCode sessions: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite; `session`/`message`/`part`/`event` tables)

- Real Claude Code sessions (including this very session's own transcript): `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`
- **CodeBurn** (`github.com/getagentseal/codeburn`, MIT licensed, npm/npx installable): a real, production, multi-orchestrator on-disk session parser covering 37 tools via `src/providers/*.ts` (includes `codex.ts`, `opencode.ts`, `opencode-file-parser.ts`, `antigravity.ts`, `claude.ts`, `kimi.ts`, `kimicode.ts`, `qwen.ts`, `sqlite-session-parser.ts` as a generic SQLite-session factory).
